title: How an agent decides it is done

items.stem: In the canonical agentic loop from the Claude API docs, with no turn cap, which condition sends the loop around for another round?

options.text: The last tool call returned no error
The model's text says it is still working

items.stem: Your agent's last response stops mid-sentence, and its stop_reason is max_tokens. What is the right reading of this ending?

options.text: The answer was cut off and is not finished
The model judged that the task was finished
The model declined to continue with the task
A server tool paused and must be resumed

items.stem: Claude is running server tools such as web search, and the server-side loop reaches its iteration limit before the work is complete. Which stop_reason value comes back in the response? Give the exact value.
An Agent SDK run is started with max_turns=5. Claude uses four tool-calling turns and then writes a final text-only answer. No budget is set and nothing errors. How does the run end?

options.text: success, with the final answer in result

items.stem: A Claude Code agent ends its turn with end_turn and writes 'All tests pass', but the transcript shows it never ran the tests. What lets you automatically refuse that stop and send it back to work with a reason?

options.text: Raising max_turns so the agent can run longer
A Stop hook that returns decision block
Raising max_tokens so the answer can be longer
Nothing, since end_turn confirms the task succeeded
